ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is solar altitude and the horizontal axis is Beijing time; there are two daily variation curves of solar altitude, a and b, and the stem states that a and b respectively represent places Q and P, so place P corresponds to curve b. In the figure, curve b rises from the point marked m on the left, its highest point is near Beijing time 14:40, and then it descends to sunset; the sunrise and sunset ranges of the two curves a and b are different, showing that the day lengths of the two places on that day are different. Reasoning: The stem gives m as Beijing time 8:40, and curve b for place P reaches the maximum solar altitude at Beijing time 14:40, that is, local noon, so for place P the interval from sunrise to local noon is 6 hours. The time from sunrise to noon is half of the day length, so the day length at place P on that day is 12 hours. Since in the figure the day lengths of places a and b on the same day are not the same, that day is not the vernal equinox or autumnal equinox when day and night are equal globally. A place that still has a day length of 12 hours on a non-equinox day can only be the equator. At the equator, direct overhead Sun occurs once each at the vernal equinox and the autumnal equinox in a year, so place P has 2 instances of direct overhead Sun in a year.
